source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Front Suspension, p.3-12

procedures.title: Front coil spring: remove and install
steps: Removal: take the nut, retainer and grommet off the top of the shock absorber.
On a hoist, support the front of the car so the control arms hang free.
Disconnect the stabilizer bar from the lower control arm; unbolt the shock from the lower arm and remove it.
Bolt tool J-22944 to a jack and place it under the lower arm so the arm bushings sit in the tool grooves (see figure 20 in the manual).
For safety, run a chain through the spring and the lower control arm.
Remove the cross shaft rear retaining nut and the two front retaining bolts.
Lower the jack slowly until the spring is free.
Take off the chain, swing the arm forward and lift out the spring.
Installation: seat the spring correctly on the control arm and raise the arm.
Align the arm to the crossmember with a large drift and fit the cross shaft retaining bolts; torque to specification.
Reconnect the stabilizer link and bolt the shock absorber to the lower arm.
Lower the car and fit the shock's upper grommet, retainer and nut.
notes: Figure 20 shows J-22944 on a jack under the Corvette lower control arm.

procedures.title: Lower control arm spherical joint: inspect
steps: Replace the lower joints whenever the upper joint inspection shows wear. Do the following only if both upper joints are within limits.
With the upper joints reconnected to the knuckles, let the car weight rest on the wheels or hubs.
Measure from the top of the lube fitting to the bottom of the ball stud with an outside micrometer or caliper; note it for each side.
Support the weight at the outer end of each lower arm so the wheels hang free and measure again.
If either side changes by more than 1/16" (.0625"), the joint is worn out: replace both lower joints.
If that passes (Chevrolet and Corvette only): clean out the lube hole in each joint and look for the liner partly or fully covering the opening; if so, replace both lower joints.

specs.what: lower joint wear limit (loaded vs unloaded change)

notes: A lower joint is loose in its housing when it is not attached to the knuckle; this is normal.
